title: Nice Weather for Ducks
year_note: On the album Lost Horizons (October 2002); released as a single on 20 January 2003.

notes.made: Fred Deakin and Nick Franglen (Franglen produced the album) built it on John Langstaff's recording of "All the Ducks", an English version of the Dutch children's song "Alle Eendjes Zwemmen in het Water". They couldn't clear Langstaff's voice, so the Scottish actor Enn Reitel re-sang the part. Franglen said later that the original's slightly unhinged charm was what drew them in, and that some of that edge went when Reitel's version replaced it.
notes.context: Lemon Jelly started out in London in 1998 on their own label, Impotent Fury, then moved to XL. Deakin co-founded the design firm Airside, which did the band's artwork and visuals. Lost Horizons went gold and was up for the 2003 Mercury Prize, and this single reached 16, their biggest. At gigs they'd swap support acts for things like a game of bingo hosted by Death.

listen_for.note: PopMatters heard chiming guitars, muted trumpets and a bouncing bassline before the duck song arrives.
That's Enn Reitel, an actor, standing in for John Langstaff because the original vocal couldn't be cleared.
The track turns into a brassy mambo band. This is the moment the panel argued over.

culture.title: All the Ducks
culture.line: It is built around John Langstaff's "All the Ducks", from the Dutch children's song. They couldn't clear his voice, so Scottish actor Enn Reitel re-sang it.

culture.title: Single, January 2003
culture.line: Released as a single on 20 January 2003, it peaked at 16 on the UK Singles Chart. Many reviews called it the stand-out on Lost Horizons.
